name: BN6's hit flag on a chip's objects
why: The hit flag BN6's chip use ORs into the chip's attack element by its icon element (the mask above) goes on with the element: the chip's objects take it as their element (+0x0E, from the family's r2), and BN6's collision setup keeps the element's high nibble apart at its +0x19 (0x08019FC4-0x08019FC8: ands #0xF0; strb [r7,#0x19]), a place BN5's layout has none of. Only the chip in use's flag, only where BN6 has it and BN5 not. An object of the fourth kind a support routine spawns keeps r2, the element, at +0x38 (the common spawn's words: r1-r4 at +0x34, +0x38, +0x3C, +4).
evidence: BN6's collision setup 0x08019FBA-0x08019FC8: the object's +0x0E, its low nibble to +2 and its high to +0x19
chip_airhoc: the puck's +0x0E and its collision data's +0x19 0x10 (Break, AirHoc's icon element) in BN6's battle alone, from its spawn (t35)
chip_nrthwind: NrthWind's wind (the fourth kind's type 0x39) +0x38 0x20 (Wind, its icon element) in BN6's battle alone
